observation.visible_scene: A close-up, static view of a stainless-steel pot filled with boiling water on a dark stovetop, with steam rising continuously. A long-handled metal spoon holds a single brown egg, initially positioned in the upper-left area of the frame, clear of the pot.
visible_changes: The spoon and the egg it carries translate downward across the sequence, moving from a position well above the pot rim (frame 1) to a position at the water surface inside the pot (frame 41); the pot itself stays fixed in the frame throughout, indicating the motion is of the spoon/egg, not the camera.
As the spoon descends, the egg approaches and then reaches the water line around the middle of the excerpt (roughly frames 18-22), where it begins to sit in the water.

The spoon bowl tilts progressively as it lowers, so that by the later frames the egg rests cradled in the tilted spoon at the surface, partially submerged, with the top of the egg still above the water.
The egg remains partially submerged near the surface, still supported by the tilted spoon, through the final frames; it is not seen sinking fully or leaving the spoon within this excerpt.
Steam continues to rise and swirl above the pot, and the water surface stays visibly agitated/bubbling the whole time.
The spoon handle remains visible entering from the left edge in every frame, shifting angle as the spoon tilts.
outside_clip_unknowns: What happened before frame 1 (how the egg came to be on the spoon) is not shown.
Whether the egg is ultimately released from the spoon and fully submerged after frame 41 is not shown.
The hand or mechanism moving the spoon is outside the frame.
uncertain_details: The exact frame of first contact between egg and water is gradual and partly obscured by steam and the spoon bowl.
The apparent tilt of the spoon could be a real rotation or partly an occlusion/angle effect; only the changing orientation of the visible spoon bowl and handle is directly supported.
